$comment: The eight declared scopes, from docs/spec/mutation-scoring.md §§4-5.
Data rather than a comment block, for two reasons. A scope's glob is its
definition and its name is only its identity, so the two have to sit beside
each other where something can compare them; and every exclusion carries a
named mechanism, which is a string a reader (and later a gate) has to be
able to find. stryker.config.mjs derives Stryker's flat `mutate` array from
this file, and scripts/mutation-scopes.ts scores each scope against it.
WARNING - `packages/core/src` is NON-RECURSIVE. It is the files directly in
that directory: 1227 mutants at 71.7%. Writing `packages/core/src/**` here
declares the union of all five core scopes instead (3301 at 66.6%), and the
other four vanish into it with their floors. The glob below is deliberate.
A file is excluded because a named mechanism puts it out of reach, or it is
not excluded. `covers/measure.ts` has no spec and stays in the denominator
anyway, because 'nothing tests it' is a gap and not a mechanism - which is
why every core scope's exclusion list is empty.
WARNING - `scripts/lib/walk.ts` is IN the scripts scope, against the spec's
own draft list, and the measurement is why. The spec put it under 'no spec
imports them'; true only of direct imports. `gates/public-build.test.ts`
imports `lib/public-build.ts`, which imports `walk.ts`, in-process - and the
run says so: 9 mutants, 6 killed. Reachability is about execution, not about
who writes the import. A reachable file stays in the denominator.
EDITING THIS FILE - a scope's identity is its declared NAME, and the number
travels with it explicitly. G38 (`mutation-scope`) makes a rename go red
rather than silent; these three rules say what the edit that clears it must
look like, because the alternative is that a floor resets and the diff reads
as a refactor:
RENAME  - a delete and an add in ONE diff, with the number visible on both
sides. `git mv packages/core/src/covers packages/core/src/cover`
is otherwise the cheapest weakening in this rollout.
SPLIT   - every child gets the parent's floor. Never a fresh start.
REMOVAL - the same visible-diff rule, plus the floors-file `notes` entry
every other lowering carries. Deleting a scope is a legitimate
fix for a zero-mutant refusal AND the cheapest way to stop
measuring an inconvenient one - and unlike lowering a floor, it
does not read as a lowering. It reads as cleanup.
EXCLUDED DIRECTORIES are the second and last state a source directory may
be in: declared, or excluded with a mechanism. There is no third. Each entry
covers the files DIRECTLY in that directory and never a subtree - a subtree
exclusion would silently swallow a declared scope beneath it, which is the
same invisible-removal move the rules above exist to close.

excludedDirectories.mechanism: `gates/repo.ts:13` is `REPO_ROOT = resolve(process.cwd())` and Stryker's sandbox is not the repository, so in a sandbox every repo-shape gate silently retargets at a copy of the tree: four gates shell out to git into a directory that is not a checkout, and G23 regex-matches source text Stryker has rewritten by construction. Mutating anything here pulls those specs in and the run dies at the dry run. Measured, and reversible on a stated condition: `REPO_ROOT` resolved from a marker rather than from `cwd`.

The files directly in it - `site-meta.ts` today - are imported only by `.astro` pages, which are not in the Vitest project, so nothing runs them in-process. Same mechanism as `shelf/start.ts`, one directory up. Non-recursive: `shelf/` below it is a declared scope.

scopes.name: packages/core/src
scopes.note: Non-recursive: the files directly in packages/core/src, not the union of the four scopes below.

exclusions.mechanism: Its only oracle is `pnpm smoke:render`, which drives a headless browser. Not a Vitest spec at all, so no in-process test ever sees the active mutant.
The page's boot chain. Reached only through `start.ts` from `Shelf.astro`, so its only oracle is the browser render.
Imported only by `packages/site/src/components/Shelf.astro`. `.astro` files are not in the Vitest project, so nothing runs it in-process.
The `?solo` turntable, imported only by `boot.ts`. Same browser-only chain.
The `?debug` panel, lazily imported by `boot.ts`. Same browser-only chain.
The black box, statically imported by `boot.ts`. Same browser-only chain.
Its only runtime importer is `scene.ts`, which the browser drives. `placement.ts` takes `Contact` as an `import type`, which is erased and carries no runtime edge.
The bloom composer, imported only by `scene.ts`. Same browser-only chain.

G14 (`commands`) reads it as source *text* via a regex and never imports it. There is no import edge, so `vitest.related` never pulls a spec in and no mutant can be killed - 435 mutants, every one NoCoverage.

Its spec `packages/cli/src/env.test.ts` calls `process.chdir()` ten times, which does not exist in a worker thread, and Stryker's vitest-runner hardcodes `pool: 'threads'`. The spec is excluded from `vitest.stryker.config.ts` to get a dry run at all, so it never sees a mutant. A property of the harness, not of the tests.

scopes.name: scripts
scopes.note: The only scope the spec left unmeasured. Measured by #155: the whole directory is 2412 mutants at 7.71%, of which 2103 are NoCoverage in files nothing runs in-process. What is left is the publisher and the directory walker it calls.

exclusions.mechanism: Its only oracle is the `spawnSync` in `gates/deploy-branch.test.ts`, which drives it as a child process under `tsx`. The child never sees the active mutant.
G24 (`repo-root`) reads it as source text via `codeOf` and never imports it. No import edge, so no mutant can be killed.
Run by `tsx` from a pnpm script (`pnpm gate:public`); never a Vitest spec. The rules it applies live in `lib/public-build.ts`, which is in this scope.
Run by `tsx` from a pnpm script (`pnpm smoke:render`), and it drives a headless browser. Never a Vitest spec.

No spec imports it — run by `tsx` from `.githooks/pre-commit`, which git invokes as a child process. Never a Vitest spec, so no in-process oracle ever sees the active mutant. The arithmetic, the join and the table it prints live in `lib/crap.ts`, which is NOT excluded: `lib/crap.test.ts` reaches every rule in-process against planted reports.
No spec imports it; its only callers are `deploy.ts`, `worktree.ts` and `crap.ts`, all excluded here.
